co_arkansas_valley_bouldering.blurb: Bouldering fills the Arkansas River valley around Buena Vista, with the high Sawatch Range on the skyline. Almost every climb here is a boulder problem, and the grades run from V0 into the double digits, with the bulk between V2 and V6, so newcomers and strong boulderers both have plenty to do. Most of the terrain sits in low, dry hills on the east side of the valley, and the east zone holds far more problems than the north, west or south zones. Rock quality is generally solid, and bouldering is possible through the whole year. In summer, afternoon thunderstorms often drift off the high peaks, so plans tend to shift around the weather. The problems are scattered across many small groups of blocks rather than one big cluster.

az_winslow_hwy_s_87_99_corridors.blurb: South of Winslow, these two highways cross a windswept high-desert plain that is cut by deep canyons exposing layers of limestone and sandstone. Sport climbing makes up most of the climbing, with a fair amount of trad and a scatter of boulders. The grades are steep: the core is 5.10 to 5.12, with a thinner tail of 5.8 and 5.9 warm-ups and a handful of 5.13 and 5.14 lines. Jacks Canyon is a shaded gorge of pocketed limestone walls around 70 feet tall, where thin crimps and small pockets set the style, and mornings stay cold well into early summer. East Clear Creek offers both trad and bolted faces, from slabby to overhanging. Powerline Crag and Chevelon Canyon are small outliers.

or_mt_hood_national_forest.blurb: A loose collection of crags and boulder fields sits in the forest surrounding Mt. Hood, though not on the mountain itself. Sport routes lead, trad is a solid second, and bouldering is also substantial; ice and alpine lines are rare here. Most roped climbs fall between 5.8 and 5.11, with the heaviest concentration at 5.10. Klinger Spring has a mix of sport and trad, Lost Lake Boulders is the main boulder hub, and French's Dome is a small andesite dome with bolted lines. The sites are spread over many separate roads and drainages, and snow and road conditions limit climbing from roughly November through April.

ca_real_hidden_valley.blurb: Real Hidden Valley is a cluster of formations in the middle of Joshua Tree National Park, where a flat, sandy valley floor is walled in by outcrops roughly 30 to 50 feet high. The rock is monzogranite, grippy and weathered into rounded boulders pocked with small cavities. Trad climbing is the main event, with a good amount of bouldering and top-roping and only a little sport. Grades span a wide range but centre on 5.9 to 5.11, with 5.10 the most common. Sentinel, Sports Challenge Rock and Turtle Rock Circuit are among the larger sub-areas. Winter and spring, roughly October to April, are the comfortable months; summer brings heat above 100 degrees with no shade.

tx_north_mountain.blurb: North Mountain is the bouldering heart of Hueco Tanks, a rocky hill rising from the desert of far West Texas, where rainwater once collected in natural basins. Nearly everything is a boulder problem, with only a sprinkling of trad, sport and top-rope. The spread is wide, from V0 up to V12 with a couple of V14s, but easier problems are numerous, with V0 to V5 making up most of the list. Holds are the namesake huecos, pockets and edges on hard, sharp rock, and crash pads are standard. Winter is prime time, roughly November through March; wind is common until spring, and from mid-April the heat sets in. Warm Up Boulder, Central Wall and Lunch Rocks are among the larger sub-areas.

ct_western_highlands.blurb: Western Highlands covers the hilly northwest of Connecticut, where getting around means a network of local roads rather than a main highway. The rock is gneiss, much of it pink and granitic. Bouldering accounts for most of the climbs, mainly V0 to V4 with a few harder problems; Burr Pond State Park and Paugnut State Forest hold several hundred big boulders of solid, fine-grained stone with friendly friction. For rope work, trad and top-rope dominate, mostly 5.6 to 5.10, with sport on only a few cliffs. Whitestone Cliffs has several crags and slabs, and St. John's Ledges offers long slab climbs that suit beginners learning to top-rope. A few ice routes form in winter.
